subject: Re: Clarify non-learning assurances and retention/archival windows
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Non-learning guarantee + retention details (initial questions)

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. Our security and procurement teams are evaluating Redwood for a pilot. Two quick but important questions we need answered in writing before we proceed:

1) Can Redwood confirm the standard wording that "you do not train models on customer data" for Hosted API customers by default? If there are exceptions (e.g., aggregated telemetry, safety improvement), please list them.

2) For retention of logs, backups, and model snapshots, what are the default retention windows, and what options do customers have to request accelerated deletion (including for snapshots and offsite backups)? In particular, our compliance team wants to know how long ephemeral inference logs and any debug snapshots are kept by default.

If helpful, we can accept a short PDF or SOC2 extract that calls this out for procurement. Hoping to get a short answer by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Security & Risk, Acme AI
laura.chen@acme.ai

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Non-learning guarantee + retention details (initial questions)

Hi Laura — good questions, and welcome. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer inference data to train or fine-tune public models by default. There are limited telemetry and safety signals (low-volume, aggregated) used to detect abuse and improve stability; those are described below. See the attached one-page summary for procurement.

Detail (hosted mode defaults):
- Non-learning guarantee: By default we do not incorporate customer inference data into training datasets or fine-tuning pipelines. If a customer explicitly opts into a managed fine-tuning service, that is documented and requires customer approval and a separate agreement.
- Telemetry: We collect operational telemetry (error rates, latencies, token counts) and lightweight anomaly signals. These are aggregated and sampled for system health and platform improvements. They are not linked back into model training datasets.
- Safety signals: In rare cases of abuse, we may store flagged examples for internal safety investigations. Those are tightly access-controlled and retained only as long as needed for the investigation.

Retention windows (hosted defaults):
- Ephemeral inference logs (request metadata, short-lived traces): 30 days
- Full request payloads (text) kept for 30 days by default; customers can request purging earlier via support ticket and an authenticated deletion workflow.
- Backups and snapshots (for disaster recovery): retained for up to 90 days by default; snapshot deletion can require an additional step to ensure consistency — we can expedite on request in most cases.
- Audit logs (security/audit events): 1 year by default for customers on standard plans; enterprise compliance plans can extend this with configurable retention.

Next steps: attaching a concise PDF summary and a SOC2 extract snippet we can share with procurement. Priyom and Naomi are cc'd to confirm wording for contracts/clauses. Happy to hop on a quick call if procurement needs it.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_nonlearning_summary.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: soc2-evidence-extract.txt (txt)

From: security@acme.ai <security@acme.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Non-learning guarantee + retention details (follow-up)

Michael — thanks for the summary. A few follow-ups from our engineering team:

1) For the 30-day full request payload retention, is that configurable per-customer or per-route? We have a routing layer where specific endpoints must not persist payload text beyond 24 hours.
2) For backups/snapshots: are there offline/offsite copies that fall outside the 90-day window (e.g., long-term archival for compliance)? If so, what is the mechanism to ensure those are purged?
3) Can you confirm whether debug snapshots (used for customer support to reproduce issues) are ever ingested into model training pipelines?

Appreciate concrete answers we can include in an internal risk memo.

—Acme Security Team

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: security@acme.ai <security@acme.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Non-learning guarantee + retention details (follow-up)

Thanks — good clarifying questions. Answers below, with how we handle hosted vs dedicated/private deployments.

1) Configurable retention per-customer/route: Hosted customers can request route-level retention policies. Our platform supports per-route overrides (24-hour TTL, 7-day TTL, 30-day TTL, etc.) for request payloads; this is a configurable setting and can be set before onboarding or via a support ticket for existing tenants. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers have direct control over retention through their deployment config (we provide the tooling and playbooks).

2) Backups/offsite archival: Default hosted policy does not put customer data into long-term cold archives without explicit org-level settings. Standard disaster recovery snapshots are retained up to 90 days and are stored in encrypted object storage. We do not copy hosted customer payloads into third-party archives for analytics. If a customer requires longer-term archival (e.g., regulatory retention), that is enacted via a customer-configured export and tracked in our export registry; those exports are customer-owned and can be deleted by the customer. We can provide written confirmation and a deletion playbook for procurement.

3) Debug snapshots and training: Debug snapshots retained for support are segregated and labeled as operational artifacts. They are not used for model training. Access is logged and limited to support and infra engineers with an explicit access justification. If a customer purchases a managed fine-tune service and explicitly provides data for training, that data path is separate and audited.

I'll paste a short suggested clause for procurement to include in a contract exhibit. Naomi / Priyom: please review the suggested wording below and confirm whether legal/security would prefer stronger language or different retention numbers.

Suggested exhibit language (draft):
"Redwood Inference Non-Learning and Retention Exhibit:
1) Redwood will not use customer inference data to train, fine-tune, or improve any public models without explicit, documented customer authorization.
2) Default hosted retention for request payloads and transient traces is thirty (30) days. Customers may request per-route TTLs (including 24-hour and 7-day options) and may request earlier deletion via Redwood support.
3) Disaster recovery snapshots are retained for up to ninety (90) days and may be expedited for deletion upon customer request, subject to operational consistency checks.
4) Operational/debug artifacts are not used in model training and are access-controlled and audited.
"

Best,
Michael

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Suggested exhibit language — legal check

Adding legal/ops voice. Quick notes: the language is good but we should avoid absolute wording like "will not" without an exception list. Suggest addition: "Except as necessary for abuse mitigation, safety investigations, or where permitted by law, Redwood will not..." Also add a line describing the deletion confirmation process (ticket, audit id, retention purge timestamp). Ben: can you validate the operational timestep for snapshot expedited deletion?

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>, security@acme.ai <security@acme.ai>

Subject: Re: Non-learning guarantee + retention details — confirmed wording and artifacts

Laura / Acme team — thanks for the patience. Naomi and Priyom reviewed and we updated the exhibit language to be procurement-ready. Attached is a one-page PDF and a small SOC2 extract you can share with procurement. Key confirmations:

- Redwood does not use customer inference data for model training or fine-tuning without explicit customer opt-in; limited exceptions for abuse/safety investigations and legal obligations are documented in the exhibit.
- Per-route TTLs are available on hosted plans; we can set a 24-hour TTL for sensitive endpoints during onboarding.
- Snapshot/backups: default 90-day retention; expedited deletion is possible — we will provide an audit ID and purge timestamp when executed.

Attached: redwood_nonlearning_summary.pdf, soc2-evidence-extract.txt

If you want, we can convert the exhibit into a DocuSign rider and attach to the SOW.

Thanks — happy to set up a short procurement call tomorrow.

Best regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference
